result.summary: Updates Chainstate::InvalidateBlock() to populate BlockValidationState with specific error messages whenever block disconnection or invalidation fails. Updates the invalidateblock RPC to explicitly reject invalidation of the genesis block and to surface InvalidateBlock() failure states as JSON-RPC errors instead of reporting success. Adds unit and functional tests covering genesis block invalidation and disconnect failures caused by corrupted undo data.
result.problem: When InvalidateBlock fails—such as when undo data is corrupted or when attempting to invalidate the genesis block—the invalidateblock RPC ignores the return value and returns null, reporting success. If block disconnection fails midway through a reorganization, callers are told the operation succeeded even though the target block was never invalidated and the chain remains only partially rolled back.
evidence: Fixes issue #36546 ('rpc: invalidateblock reports success when a block can't be disconnected')
PR description notes that when undo data is corrupt, 'the chain remains partially rolled back when telling the user that the operation succeeded'
result.changed_since_previous: Diff is now available, showing concrete BlockValidationState error strings in Chainstate::InvalidateBlock, a genesis check in RPC, and functional test coverage that flips bits in rev00000.dat.
result.card: Makes the invalidateblock RPC return an error when block disconnection or invalidation fails instead of returning success. Currently, if an error occurs while disconnecting blocks during an invalidation (such as corrupted undo data) or when attempting to invalidate the genesis block, the RPC returns null despite the chain remaining partially rolled back and the requested block remaining valid (issue #36546). The change records detailed error messages into BlockValidationState, propagates them as JSON-RPC errors, and adds test coverage for partial rollback and genesis block errors.

risk.why: Mistakes in InvalidateBlock error paths could alter chainstate rollback behavior or misreport chain status during manual node recovery.
